newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bourse delays stricter force sale rules.
newsitem.headline: Thai bourse delays stricter force sale rules.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) on Thursday reacted to heavy falls in Thai stocks this month by announcing a six-month delay in adopting stricter rules that force indebted investors to sell stocks to help them meet margin calls.
SET president Singh Tangtatswas told reporters the bourse decided to postpone a January 1 deadline for enforcing the market's maintenance margin rules to July 1, 1997.
Thai stocks have been hammered this month with the composite SET Index losing 93.37 points, or 10.1 percent, since December 2. It finished at a 42-month low of 832.60 points on Thursday.
The last time the index closed lower was on June 8, 1993, when it ended at 830.71.

The SET had originally planned from January 1 to force investors who borrowed on margin from brokerage firms, to sell their holdings if their market prices fell below 25 percent of the collaterised margins of their loans.
According to current, more lenient, rules hard-pressed investors are not forced to sell shares until their market prices dip below 15 percent.

Singh dismissed as moderate the forced sale transactions this week that averaged 40 million baht a day. He said active selling by Thai and foreign investors this week reflected the market's negative perception of the Thai economy and the country's current account deficit.
Earlier this week Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond predicted the current account deficit would be 8.2 percent of gross domestic product this year against 8.1 percent in 1995.
